A single greedy arm therefore carries about 2.5 tasks of standard deviation and a paired p-value over one run per arm overstates its precision.

The same task-derived request, sent greedily with the protocol seed echoed by the server: 5 sequential requests at one row per step returned 1 distinct completion token sequence with bitwise identical per-token log-probabilities, while 6 or 8 requests sent at once returned 2 distinct sequences with the first divergent token at 7 and 2 at once returned 1. A never-seen prompt sent once cold and then twice warm was identical, yet six concurrent copies of it gave 3 distinct sequences at the record's 2444-token prompt and 5 at about four times that length. So a single-row decode is reproducible and a row's arithmetic depends on its co-batch: the int8 projections switch to a tensor-core block from five rows and the fused decode attention sizes its split count from the batch. Concurrency alone does not make an episode reproducible - the same adapter on the same 8 tasks, greedy with one request in flight, passed 3 then 5 of 8 with 2 verdicts flipped, and a concurrency-8 run of the same arm passed 5 with 2 verdicts different from the first.
